tldr: Three unrelated arXiv papers share the word routing: expert routing for respiratory-sound classifiers under device drift (Oct 20), then strategy-guided RL for picking agent skills (Oct 30). The link is vocabulary, not a continuing research line.
whats_new: A Nov 4 arXiv paper learns which visual tokens a computer-use agent keeps, targeting the compute cost of long-horizon and real-time agent tasks.
why_it_matters: Learned routing is showing up in agent cost control (skills, tokens), but these are single-paper claims with no shared benchmark or released tooling.

status.detail: Three papers from two arXiv feeds reuse the routing idea in different domains; no cross-citation or common evaluation is shown.

beats.headline: Expert routing for respiratory-sound domain-incremental learning
TalentRL applies strategy-guided RL to hierarchical skill routing for LLM agents
Visual Token Routing learns which tokens computer-use agents keep

open_questions: Do TalentRL or Visual Token Routing release code or report results on a public agent benchmark?
Does the token-routing paper report a measured compute or latency reduction for computer-use agents?
take_for_builders: Treat these as ideas to watch: if you run computer-use agents, wait for reproducible cost numbers before changing token or skill selection.
